title: How do you optimize a slow SQL query in production?
description: Analyze execution plans, add indexes, and avoid table scans.

data.text: **Question:** How do you optimize a slow SQL query in production?
Analyze the execution plan, add covering indexes, rewrite joins or subqueries, and consider query caching or materialized views.

items: Execution plan: look for table scans, key lookups, and sorts
Indexes: add nonclustered indexes on filtered columns
SARGability: avoid functions on indexed columns in WHERE
Pagination: use keyset pagination instead of OFFSET
Caching: query cache or Redis for repeated reads

data.code:
-- Before: non-sargable
SELECT * FROM Orders
WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2024;

-- After: sargable
SELECT * FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' 
  AND OrderDate < '2025-01-01';

-- Covering index
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Orders_OrderDate
ON Orders(OrderDate)
INCLUDE (CustomerId, Total);

items: Adding too many indexes without measuring write impact
Using SELECT * when only a few columns are needed
When do you use a materialized view?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Pagination should use keyset for large offsets
